page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the n4d server family. It features 2 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage options for persistent data.

The instance operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires external networking configurations or NAT gateways for public internet connectivity. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated graphics hardware positions this instance as a specialized memory-dense node rather than a storage-heavy or acceleration-dependent server. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without the performance fluctuations associated with shared-core or burstable instances.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4d-highmem-2 provides a high memory-to-vCPU density within its hardware class, allowing memory-intensive applications to run without the need to provision excess compute cores. This resource balance is suitable for workloads such as small-scale databases, caching layers, memory-bound enterprise applications, and lightweight data processing tasks that require substantial memory capacity relative to processing power.
